steps.body: An L-shaped figure isn't a single rectangle — but it splits into two. Cut it with one straight line and you get a bottom rectangle and a top rectangle; **add their areas** for the total. A 10-by-8 L with a 4-by-3 corner missing splits into a 10×5 rectangle (50) plus a 6×3 rectangle (18): total **68**.

widget.prompt: An L-shape splits into a 6×4 rectangle and a 3×2 rectangle. What is the total area?

commonErrors.feedback: 24 is only the BIGGER piece (6×4), leaving out the 3×2 piece entirely. Add both: 24 + 6 = 30.
144 multiplies the two pieces together instead of adding them. Combining pieces of one shape means ADDING: 24 + 6 = 30.

predict.prompt: An L-shape has no formula of its own. Can its area still be found exactly?

options.label: Yes — cut it into rectangles and add

predict.reveal: Any straight-sided shape splits into rectangles — find each piece's area and add. Decomposing beats memorizing a formula for every shape.

widget.prompt: An L-shape splits into an 8×3 rectangle and a 5×4 rectangle. What is the total area?

commonErrors.feedback: 20 is only the second piece (5×4), missing the 8×3 piece. Add both: 24 + 20 = 44.
480 multiplies the two piece-areas together. Combine by ADDING: 24 + 20 = 44.

steps.body: There's a second, equally valid path: picture the L-shape's **bounding box** — the full rectangle it would be without the missing corner — then **subtract the cut-out** piece. The 10-by-8 example: bounding box 10×8 = 80, minus the 4×3 cut = 12, giving 80 − 12 = 68. Same answer, different route — a genuine check on your work.

explanationVariants: Bounding box 6×6 = 36, minus the 3×2 cut (6): 36 − 6 = 30 — matching the addition method exactly.

widget.prompt: The same L-shape from before has a 6×6 bounding box with a 3×2 corner cut out. Using SUBTRACTION, what is the total area?

commonErrors.feedback: 36 is just the bounding box, forgetting to subtract the cut-out corner: 36 − 6 = 30.
42 ADDS the cut instead of subtracting it. A missing corner is REMOVED: 36 − 6 = 30.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 36 − 6 = 30 — the bounding box minus the cut-out corner.

widget.prompt: Each L-shape description should give the SAME area both ways. Match each to its total.

pairErrors.feedback: 8×7 − 3×4 = 56 − 12 = 44, not 68. That's the SAME L-shape as the 8×3-and-5×4 split.

widget.missFeedback: Compute each description: subtraction gives bounding box minus cut; addition gives the two rectangle pieces summed. Two descriptions describe the SAME shape.
widget.successFeedback: Matched — subtraction and addition describe the same two L-shapes, landing on the same two totals.

explanationVariants: Either method works: bounding 9×6 (54) minus cut 3×2 (6) = 48; or rectangles 9×4 (36) plus 6×2 (12) = 48.
Both routes land on 48 — pick whichever is easier to picture.

widget.prompt: An L-shape has a 9×6 bounding box with a 3×2 corner missing. Find its area using either method.

commonErrors.feedback: 54 is just the bounding box, forgetting the cut: 54 − 6 = 48.
60 ADDS the cut area instead of removing it. A missing corner subtracts: 54 − 6 = 48.

hints: Or split into two rectangles and add — both should agree.
explanationVariants: Bounding 12×9 = 108, minus cut 5×4 = 20: 108 − 20 = 88. (Equivalently, two rectangles would also sum to 88.)

widget.prompt: An L-shaped patio has a 12×9 bounding box with a 5×4 corner missing (a flower bed). What is the patio's area?

commonErrors.feedback: 108 is the full bounding box, forgetting to remove the flower bed corner: 108 − 20 = 88.
128 ADDS the corner instead of subtracting it. The missing corner is REMOVED: 108 − 20 = 88.

takeaways: Split an L-shape into two rectangles and ADD their areas.
Or take the bounding box and SUBTRACT the missing corner — same answer either way.
Using both methods on the same shape is a built-in check on your work.
steps.teaser: next: composite figures built with triangles, not just rectangles.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Two rectangles, added — or bounding box, minus the cut.** A 5×5 bounding box with a 2×2 corner missing: 25 − 4 = 21. Or split into pieces that also sum to 21. Either way works.

explanationVariants: Bounding box minus the missing corner: 21.

widget.prompt: An L-shape has a 5×5 bounding box with a 2×2 corner missing. What is its area?

commonErrors.feedback: 25 is just the bounding box. Subtract the missing corner: 25 − 4 = 21.
29 adds the corner instead of subtracting it. A missing piece is REMOVED: 25 − 4 = 21.
